newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House re-elects Gingrich as speaker.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House re-elects Gingrich as speaker.

text.p: Newt Gingrich was re-elected speaker of the House of Representatives by Republican backers on Tuesday despite admitted ethics violations that led a few party colleagues to try to dump him.

The vote in the opening session of the 105th U.S. Congress, elected last November, was 216 for Gingrich, 205 for Minority Leader Richard Gephardt of Missouri, a Democrat, and four scattered for other Republicans with six voting "present." That gave the controversial Gingrich, 53, a slim majority of those voting and a second two-year term as House speaker.

It is the third-ranking elective office in the United States, afther the president and vice president, but Gingrich had been in danger of losing it since he admitted last month to breaches of House ethics rules.

Republicans told reporters he apologised to his House party colleagues for his "mistakes" during one last attempt to rally support shortly before the House vote that spared him the humiliation of being ousted from the speakership.

The House Ethics Committee is scheduled to begin on Wednesday a consideration of possible punishments, which would be voted upon by the full House in about two weeks. It was widely expected he would be reprimanded for admitting he gave false information to House investigators and for failing to ensure that tax-exempt donations were not used in a college course he taught. Critics say the course involved partisan politcs.
